basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: Models the act of releasing content to channels, not the content, work or edition itself.
Keeps approval, release instruction, delivery, propagation and availability as separate states.
Records corrections, retractions and takedowns as new events with notices.
Binds rights, licence and accessibility clearances to each release.

may: Package approved content with metadata for each channel.
Verify that releases arrived and render correctly.
Monitor availability and report broken or stale copies.
Prepare correction notices for editorial review.
mustNot: Publish without the required editorial and rights clearance.
Silently change published content without a correction notice.
Publish personal data or embargoed material.
Report syndication or reach as approval or quality.
Remove content on an unverified takedown request.
requiresHuman: Clearance of rights, defamation or privacy risks.

considerations: Published content can harm reputations and privacy; corrections must be visible and timely.
Accessibility determines who can use the content.
Takedown handling must balance rights holders against freedom of expression.
affectedParties: People named or shown in content

items: A publication case has target content, a release version, channels, clearances and a release time.
It is confused with the content itself, a publication edition or a social media post.
Defamation or privacy harm from unchecked releases.
Stale copies persisting after a correction.
Accidental early release of embargoed content.
Crossref metadata and DOI for scholarly publications.
